title: Cannot Snap Child Window on W10 Outlook Reminders

judgment.rationale: The report provides Outlook builds, Windows versions, a diagnostic archive and a control comparison. A popup-versus-owned-window eligibility test is more useful than requesting the same evidence again.
evidence: Outlook Reminders does not show zones during Shift-drag, while the main Outlook window does.
Reported on Windows 10 with PowerToys 0.76.2 and Windows 11 with 0.79.0; toggling child-window snapping and elevation did not resolve it.
Related #32660 was explicitly closed into this issue; manually adding the old popup setting had no effect.
Current DefineWindowType rejects some WS_POPUP windows before applying allowSnapChildWindows.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the Reminders window classification and consider a narrowly tested dialog-eligibility correction.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete implementation is linked. The child-window setting cannot override an earlier popup rejection in current classification.

proposed_fixes.title: Distinguish snappable Outlook dialogs from transient popup menus
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: Reminders is rejected by the root/style/popup eligibility checks before the owned-window setting is considered. Its actual HWND styles and rejection reason have not been captured in this pass.
plan: Trace FancyZonesWindowProcessing::DefineWindowType for Outlook Reminders and compare with the main window while allowSnapChildWindows is enabled.
If a legitimate movable dialog is rejected by popup classification, refine that predicate or explicit dialog handling without accepting menus, tooltips, notification windows or controls.
Add window-style predicate tests and cover both settings states, Outlook main windows and transient popup exclusions.
verification: Shift-drag the Reminders window with child-window snapping enabled: zones appear and the dialog snaps.
With the setting disabled, verify the intended owned-window behavior; menus and dropdowns never snap.
Repeat on current Outlook/Windows and the reported configurations if available.

confidence.rationale: The reports and current ordering fit a classification issue, but the target window's rejected predicate is unverified.

issue_context.summary: Outlook Reminders stopped activating FancyZones during Shift-drag after older updates; the main Outlook window still works, across both Windows 10 and 11 reports.
known_information: The original report includes a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP and Outlook 2311/Windows 10 build details.
A later update supplies Windows 11 23H2, PowerToys 0.79.0 and Outlook 2402.
Child-window setting toggles and running as administrator were already tried.
The issue is open and unassigned.
inferences: A window-type eligibility regression is plausible; child-window and popup classifications are not interchangeable.
The contrary symptom in #33450 concerns some owned windows snapping when disabled and is not proof of the same defect.
issue_context.analysis: Use the existing reproduction and control to trace classification locally. Do not repeat the ineffective legacy allowPopupWindowSnap configuration advice from related discussion.
initial_investigation: Read the body, all three comments and paginated timeline; inspected #32660 and #33450.

Inspected src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/FancyZonesWindowProcessing.cpp at main commit 3d6827a53a579ba9bedcf8d4bbda21348d78cbdb: non-root and popup filtering precede the visible-owner child-window setting.
No Outlook session, HWND capture or native build was executed; no resolution is claimed.

reproduce.title: Compare Reminders and main-window Shift-drag
reproduce.version_requirement: Current PowerToys and classic Outlook; reported baselines are 0.76.2/Outlook 2311 and 0.79.0/Outlook 2402.
prerequisites: Classic Outlook with a test reminder and at least one configured FancyZones layout; use a test profile.
steps: 1. Enable child-window snapping and open Outlook Reminders from a test reminder.
2. Shift-drag the main Outlook window as a positive control, then Shift-drag Reminders.
3. Record the Reminders HWND styles, owner/root relationship and DefineWindowType return value.
4. Repeat with child-window snapping disabled and with a normal dropdown to test negative controls.
5. Test the smallest classification change against both windows and popup-menu exclusions.
reproduce.expected_result: Eligible owned dialogs snap according to the setting, while transient menus and controls remain excluded.
